full_judgment: 2. The respondent No. 1 Arab Bangladesh Bank Limited, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 134 of 1995 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka against the defendant Nos. 1 to 5 for realization of outstanding loan. That suit was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 143 of 1998. The suit was ultimately decreed ex-parts vide judgment and decree dated 25.11.1998. Since the judgment debtor failed to pay the decretal amount within the prescribed time the decree holder hank put that decree into execution in Title Execution Case No. 99 of 2000. In that execution case the mortgaged properties were put in auction as many as five times but could not be sold as none of the price offered was satisfactory. Lastly on 14.01.2003 the mortgaged properties were again put in auction and this time six bidders participated in that auction and the highest bid offered for schedule "A" property was Tk. 27,00,000/- and for the schedule "B" property was Tk. 60,01,000/-. The executing court accepted the said highest bid' and ultimately on receipt of the entire auction money from the highest bidder made the auction sale absolute. Meanwhile with the proclamation of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the said title execution case was renumbered as Title Execution Case No. 3 of 2003 and was transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka for disposal in this Adalat the sale deed was executed and registered as per clue process of law on 10.07.2003 and the possession also of this auction sold property was delivered to the auction purchaser. Thereafter on 30.08.2003 the present petitioner Mrs. Jahanara Ahmed filed an application under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the sale of the "B" schedule property and that application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2003 which was subsequently renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2003. The case of this petitioner was that she purchased the “B” schedule property from Hossain Ahmed Chowdhury the judgment debtor at a consideration of Tk. 10,00,000/-. That she made payment of full consideration money to Hossain Ahmed Chowdhury and got possession of the "B" schedule property with one storied building standing thereon. That subsequently both the vendor and vendee made prayer to the Cantonment Board, Dhaka on 16.10.1985 for permission of the said transfer. Ultimately having obtained permission on 01.08.1988 from the Cantonment Board Mr. Hossain Ahmed Chowdhury executed a sale deed in favour of the appellant on 10.06.1988. But since the executant was found absent the sub-registrar, (Gulshan, Dhaka refused to register the same. and as such Refusal Case No. 8 of 1988 was started. But ultimately it was rejected. Challenging the said rejection order the petitioner filed Appeal No. 3 of 1988 before the District Registrar, Dhaka and the District Registrar, Dhaka allowed that appeal and consequently the said sale deed was registered in the year 1990 with effect from 08.09.1988. Thereafter the petitioner prayed before the Secretary, Ministry of Defence for mutation of her name, but that prayer was rejected with a direction upon this petitioner to file a regular suit before the court of law. Accordingly the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 87 of 2003 before the court of Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka which was dismissed on 02.03.2005. Against this dismissal order the petitioner filed appeal which is still pending. Later there was an amicable settlement between the petitioner and the wife of Hossain Ahmed Chowdhury, namely, Mrs. Dilruba Hussain Chowdhury and accordingly the petitioner filed an application before the Cantonment Board, Dhaka for mutation of her name. During pendency of the said mutation case the petitioner cane to know about the auction sale of her purchased land and then she filed the application under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the auction sale on the ground of fraud and material irregularity.
